content: The text provided is a list of references formatted in a non-standard way, likely extracted from a bibliography or citation list. It includes studies, reviews, and guidelines related to hepatitis C, HIV co-infection, and various treatment regimens. 1. E et al. conducted a Cochrane Review in 2013, focusing on psychosocial interventions aimed at reducing alcohol consumption among individuals who concurrently use alcohol and illicit drugs. The findings were published in Systematic Reviews, volume 2, article 3. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) developed the ASSIST package in 2011, a tool designed to address substance abuse. This resource is accessible online and was last accessed on January 30, 2014. 3. The WHO also published the mhGAP intervention guide in 2010, which provides strategies for managing mental, neurological, and substance use disorders in non-specialized healthcare settings. This guide was accessed on January 21, 2014. 4. The French METAVIR Cooperative Study Group examined intraobserver and interobserver variability in liver biopsy interpretation for patients with chronic hepatitis C. Their findings were published in Hepatology in 1994, volume 20, pages 15–20. 5. Scheuer PJ proposed a reassessment of the classification system for chronic viral hepatitis in 1991, as detailed in the Journal of Hepatology, volume 13, pages 372–374. 6. Ishak K et al. introduced a histological grading and staging system for chronic hepatitis in 1995, published in the Journal of Hepatology, volume 22, pages 696–699. 7. Bedossa P and Poynard T developed an algorithm for grading activity in chronic hepatitis C, as part of the METAVIR Cooperative Study Group. This was published in Hepatology in 1996, volume 24, pages 289–293. 8. Batts KP and Ludwig J provided an update on terminology and reporting for chronic hepatitis in 1995, published in the American Journal of Surgical Pathology, volume 19, pages 1409–1417. 9. Knodell RG et al. formulated a numerical scoring system to assess histological activity in asymptomatic chronic active hepatitis. This was published in Hepatology in 1981, volume 1, pages 431–435. 10. Lin ZH et al. evaluated the performance of the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) for staging hepatitis C-related fibrosis. Their meta-analysis was published in Hepatology in 2011, volume 53, pages 726–736. 11. Sterling RK et al. developed a simple non-invasive index to predict significant fibrosis in patients with HIV/HCV co-infection. This study was published in Hepatology in 2006, volume 43, pages 1317–1325. 12. Malaguarnera M et al. conducted a meta-analytic evaluation of interferon-alpha treatment in patients with chronic hepatitis C. Their findings were published in Clinical Drug Investigation in 1995, volume 9, pages 141–149. 13. Myers RP and Poynard T reviewed the use of interferon for non-responding and relapsing patients with chronic hepatitis C. This Cochrane Database Systematic Review was published in 2002, issue 4, article CD003617. 14. Hu J et al. systematically reviewed the treatment of hepatitis C in children, with findings published in PLoS One in 2010, volume 5, article e11542. 15. Koretz RL et al. reviewed interferon therapy for non-responding and relapsing patients with chronic hepatitis C. This Cochrane Database Systematic Review was published in 2013, issue 1, article CD003617. 16. Tine F et al. conducted a meta-regression analysis of interferon-alpha trials for chronic hepatitis C over a decade. Their findings were published in Contemporary Clinical Trials in 2005, volume 26, pages 179–210. 17. Carithers RL Jr and Emerson SS performed a meta-analysis of interferon alfa-2b trials for hepatitis C therapy. This was published in Hepatology in 1997, volume 26, supplement 1, pages S83–S88. 18. Fabrizi F et al. analyzed antiviral therapy for hepatitis C in chronic kidney disease patients. Their meta-analysis was published in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2008, volume 15, pages 600–606. 19. Xirouchakis E et al. reviewed the use of pegylated-interferon and ribavirin in liver transplant candidates and recipients with HCV cirrhosis. Their systematic review and meta-analysis were published in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2008, volume 15, pages 699–709. 20. Kimer N et al. evaluated antiviral therapy for preventing hepatocellular carcinoma in chronic hepatitis C patients. Their systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials were published in BMJ Open in 2012. 21. Iorio A et al. reviewed antiviral treatment for chronic hepatitis C in HIV-infected patients. This Cochrane Database Systematic Review was published in 2010, issue 1, article CD004888. 22. Hartwell D and Shepherd J conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of pegylated and non-pegylated interferon-alpha and ribavirin for mild chronic hepatitis C. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care in 2009, volume 25, pages 56–62. 23. Vezali E et al. reviewed the treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus infection in cirrhosis. Their findings were published in Clinical Therapeutics in 2010, volume 32, pages 2117–2138. 24. Brok J et al. reviewed ribavirin monotherapy for chronic hepatitis C. This Cochrane Database Systematic Review was published in 2009, issue 4, article CD005527. 25. Aspinall EJ et al. reviewed the treatment of hepatitis C virus infection among people actively injecting drugs. Their systematic review and meta-analysis were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2013, volume 57, supplement 2, pages S80–S89. 26. Morgan TR et al. examined the outcomes of sustained virological responders with histologically advanced chronic hepatitis C. Their findings were published in Hepatology in 2010, volume 52, pages 833–844. 27. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) published a technical landscape on the diagnosis and treatment of hepatitis C in 2013. This resource is available online. 28. Carrat F et al. compared pegylated interferon alfa-2b versus standard interferon alfa-2b, both with ribavirin, for chronic hepatitis C in HIV-infected patients. Their randomized controlled trial was published in JAMA in 2004, volume 292, pages 2839–2848. 29. Chung RT et al. compared peginterferon alfa-2a plus ribavirin versus interferon alfa-2a plus ribavirin for chronic hepatitis C in HIV-co-infected individuals. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2004, volume 351, pages 451–459. 30. Torriani FJ et al. evaluated peginterferon alfa-2a plus ribavirin for chronic hepatitis C virus infection in HIV-infected patients. Their study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2004, volume 351, pages 438–450. 31. Bacon BR et al. assessed boceprevir for previously treated chronic HCV genotype 1 infection. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2011, volume 364, pages 1207–1217. 32. Hezode C et al. reported on the real-life safety of telaprevir or boceprevir in combination with peginterferon alfa/ribavirin in cirrhotic non-responders. Initial results from the French early access program (ANRS C020-CUPIC) were published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2012, volume 56, supplement 2, page S4. 33. Hezode C et al. evaluated triple therapy in treatment-experienced patients with HCV-cirrhosis in a multicenter cohort of the French Early Access Programme (ANRS CO20-CUPIC). Their findings were published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2013, volume 59, pages 434–441. 34. The British HIV Association published guidelines in 2013 for managing hepatitis viruses in adults infected with HIV. These guidelines are available online. 35. Sofosbuvir and peginterferon alfa-2a/ribavirin were evaluated for treatment-naïve genotype 1–4 HCV-infected patients co-infected with HIV. Results were presented at the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) meeting in 2013. 36. Osinusi A et al. conducted a randomized clinical trial on sofosbuvir and ribavirin for hepatitis C genotype 1 in patients with unfavorable treatment characteristics. Their findings were published in JAMA in 2013, volume 310, pages 804–811. 37. Zeuzem S et al. evaluated sofosbuvir and ribavirin for 12 or 24 weeks in patients with HCV genotype 2 or 3. Results from the VALENCE trial were presented at the 64th annual meeting of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) in 2013. 38. Simeprevir (TMC435) plus peginterferon/ribavirin was evaluated in patients co-infected with HCV genotype 1 and HIV-1. Primary analysis of the C212 study was presented at the 14th European AIDS Conference (EACS) in 2013. 39. Tanaka Y et al. conducted a genome-wide association study of IL28B with response to pegylated interferon-alpha and ribavirin therapy for chronic hepatitis C. Their findings were published in Nature Genetics in 2009, volume 41, pages 1105–1109. 40. Thomas DL et al. investigated genetic variation in IL28B and its association with spontaneous clearance of hepatitis C virus. Their study was published in Nature in 2009, volume 461, pages 798–801. 41. Mauss S et al. identified risk factors for hepatic decompensation in patients with HIV/HCV co-infection and liver cirrhosis during interferon-based therapy. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2004, volume 18, pages F21–F25. 42. Bani-Sadr F et al. reported on spontaneous hepatic decompensation in patients co-infected with HIV and hepatitis C virus during interferon-ribavirin combination treatment. Their study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2005, volume 41, pages 1806–1809. 43. Roche provided product information on Pegasys, which was accessed in January 2014. 44. Merck Canada released a product monograph on Pegatron in 2013, which was accessed in January 2014. 45. Ramos B et al. highlighted the critical role of ribavirin in achieving early virological response to HCV therapy in HCV/HIV co-infected patients. Their findings were published in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2007, volume 14, pages 387–391. 46. The WHO published guidance in 2012 on preventing viral hepatitis B and C among people who inject drugs. This resource is available online. 47. Visconti AJ et al. assessed the cost-effectiveness of treating chronic hepatitis C virus in people who inject drugs in Australia. Their findings were published in the Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2013, volume 28, pages 707–716. 48. Hellard M et al. reviewed hepatitis C treatment for injection drug users, summarizing available evidence. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2009, volume 49, pages 561–573. 49. Thein HH et al. conducted a meta-analysis on the natural history of hepatitis C virus infection in HIV-infected individuals and the impact of HIV in the era of highly active antiretroviral therapy. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2008, volume 22, pages 1979–1991. 50. Avidan NU et al. studied hepatitis C viral kinetics during treatment with peg-IFN-alpha-2b in HIV/HCV co-infected patients as a function of baseline CD4+ T-cell counts. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2009, volume 52, pages 452–458. 51. Gilead Sciences provided full prescribing information for Sovaldi in 2013, which was accessed in January 2014. 52. The FDA approved Olysio (simeprevir) for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C in combination with antiviral therapy in 2013. This information is available online. 53. The WHO released consolidated guidelines in 2013 on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection, emphasizing a public health approach. This document is accessible online. 54. Den Brinker M et al. investigated hepatitis B and C virus co-infection and the risk of hepatotoxicity associated with highly active antiretroviral therapy in HIV-1 infection. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2000, volume 14, pages 2895–2902. 55. Sulkowski MS et al. studied hepatotoxicity associated with protease inhibitor-based antiretroviral regimens with or without concurrent ritonavir. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2004, volume 19, pages 2277–2284. 56. Sulkowski MS et al. examined hepatotoxicity associated with nevirapine or efavirenz-containing antiretroviral therapy, focusing on the role of hepatitis C and B infections. Their findings were published in Hepatology in 2002, volume 35, pages 182–189. 57. Nunez M reviewed clinical syndromes and consequences of antiretroviral-related hepatotoxicity. This review was published in Hepatology in 2010, volume 52, pages 1143–1155. 58. Japour AJ et al. conducted a phase-1 study on the safety, pharmacokinetics, and antiviral activity of combination didanosine and ribavirin in patients with HIV-1 disease. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes and Human Retrovirology in 1996, volume 13, pages 235–246. 59. Harvie P et al. demonstrated that ribavirin potentiates the efficacy and toxicity of 2',3'-dideoxyinosine in a murine AIDS model. Their findings were published in the Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics in 1996, volume 279, pages 1009–1017. 60. Perronne C reviewed interactions between antiviral hepatitis and antiretroviral drugs. This review was published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2006, volume 44, supplement 1, pages S119–S125. 61. Alvarez D et al. found that zidovudine use, but not weight-based ribavirin dosing, impacts anemia during HCV treatment in HIV-infected individuals. Their findings were published in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2006, volume 13, pages 683–689. 62. Mira JA et al. evaluated the efficacy of pegylated interferon plus ribavirin treatment in HIV/hepatitis C virus co-infected patients receiving abacavir plus lamivudine or tenofovir plus either lamivudine or emtricitabine as nucleoside analogue backbones. Their findings were published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2008, volume 62, pages 1365–1373. 63. Vispo E et al. reported low response rates to pegylated interferon plus ribavirin in HIV-infected patients with HCV co-infection.
